nodes.summary: Let $f_0 = 0$ and let $f_{k+1}$ be the image of $f_k$ under the Fibonacci morphism ($0 \mapsto 01$, $1 \mapsto 0$). For all natural numbers $m$ and $n$ such that $n$ is less than the length of $f_m$, the letter of $f_m$ at index $n$ equals the letter at index $n$ of the one-sided infinite Fibonacci word (indices start at $0$). In other words, every $f_m$ is a prefix of the infinite Fibonacci word.
nodes.title: Finite Fibonacci words agree with the infinite Fibonacci word

nodes.summary: Let $f_0 = 0$ and let $f_{k+1}$ be the image of $f_k$ under the Fibonacci morphism ($0 \mapsto 01$, $1 \mapsto 0$). For every natural number $n$, the length of $f_{n+2}$ is greater than $n$.
nodes.title: The finite Fibonacci word of index $n + 2$ has more than $n$ letters

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the infinite Fibonacci word and let $f_0, f_1, f_2, \ldots$ be the finite Fibonacci words. For every natural number $N$, the finite word $w_N = 0\,1\,f_0 f_1 \cdots f_{N-1}$ (so $w_0 = 01$) consists of the first $|w_N|$ letters of $f$, and for every natural number $k$ the first $k$ letters of $f$ form a prefix of $w_N$ for some $N$. In this sense $f = 0 \cdot 1 \cdot f_0 \cdot f_1 \cdot f_2 \cdots$.
nodes.title: Factorization of the infinite Fibonacci word into finite Fibonacci words

nodes.summary: Let $f_0 = 0$ and let $f_{k+1}$ be the image of $f_k$ under the Fibonacci morphism ($0 \mapsto 01$, $1 \mapsto 0$), so that $f_0, f_1, f_2, \ldots$ are the finite Fibonacci words $0, 01, 010, 01001, \ldots$. The one-sided infinite Fibonacci word is the infinite binary word whose letter at index $n$ (indices start at $0$) is the letter of $f_{n+2}$ at index $n$.
nodes.title: Infinite Fibonacci word

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the Fibonacci morphism on finite binary words, induced by $0 \mapsto 01$ and $1 \mapsto 0$. For all finite binary words $a$ and $b$, $\varphi(ab) = \varphi(a)\varphi(b)$, where juxtaposition denotes concatenation.
nodes.title: The Fibonacci morphism respects concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the Fibonacci morphism on finite binary words, induced by $0 \mapsto 01$ and $1 \mapsto 0$. For every finite binary word $w$, the length of $\varphi(w)$ is at least the length of $w$, that is, $|w| \le |\varphi(w)|$.
nodes.title: The Fibonacci morphism does not shorten words

nodes.summary: The Fibonacci morphism $\varphi$ extends the Fibonacci substitution $\sigma$, which maps $0$ to $01$ and $1$ to $0$, to finite binary words by concatenation: $\varphi$ maps the empty word to the empty word, and $\varphi(bw) = \sigma(b)\varphi(w)$ for every letter $b$ and every finite binary word $w$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci morphism

nodes.summary: The Fibonacci substitution sends each letter of the binary alphabet $\{0, 1\}$ to a finite binary word: it maps $0$ to $01$ and $1$ to $0$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci substitution

nodes.summary: Let $f_0, f_1, f_2, \ldots$ be the finite Fibonacci words. For every natural number $n$, $f_{n+2} = f_{n+1} f_n$, where juxtaposition denotes concatenation.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the finite Fibonacci words

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the finite Fibonacci word $f_n$ is the word formed by the first $|f_n|$ letters of the infinite Fibonacci word.
nodes.title: Finite Fibonacci words are prefixes of the infinite Fibonacci word

nodes.summary: For every natural number $N$, prepending the letters $0$ and $1$ to the concatenation $f_0 f_1 \cdots f_{N-1}$ of the first $N$ finite Fibonacci words gives $f_{N+1}$: that is, $0\,1\,f_0 f_1 \cdots f_{N-1} = f_{N+1}$, where the concatenation is empty when $N = 0$.
nodes.title: Concatenating the finite Fibonacci words

nodes.summary: Let $f_0 = 0$ and let $f_{k+1}$ be the image of $f_k$ under the Fibonacci morphism ($0 \mapsto 01$, $1 \mapsto 0$). For all natural numbers $n \le m$ and every index $i$ less than the length of $f_n$ (indices start at $0$), the letter of $f_m$ at index $i$ equals the letter of $f_n$ at index $i$.
nodes.title: Letters of the finite Fibonacci words stabilize

nodes.summary: Let $f_0 = 0$ and let $f_{k+1}$ be the image of $f_k$ under the Fibonacci morphism ($0 \mapsto 01$, $1 \mapsto 0$). For every natural number $n$, there is a finite binary word $t$ such that $f_n = 0t$, that is, the first letter of $f_n$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Finite Fibonacci words begin with $0$

nodes.summary: Let $f_0 = 0$ and let $f_{k+1}$ be the image of $f_k$ under the Fibonacci morphism ($0 \mapsto 01$, $1 \mapsto 0$). For every natural number $n$, the word $f_n$ has length at least $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Lower bound on the length of the finite Fibonacci words

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th finite Fibonacci word $f_n$ is a prefix of $f_{n+1}$: there is a finite word $t$ in the letters $0$ and $1$ with $f_{n+1} = f_n t$.
nodes.title: Consecutive finite Fibonacci words are nested

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n \le m$, the $n$-th finite Fibonacci word $f_n$ is a prefix of the $m$-th finite Fibonacci word $f_m$: there is a finite word $t$ in the letters $0$ and $1$ with $f_m = f_n t$.
nodes.title: Earlier finite Fibonacci words are prefixes of later ones

nodes.summary: The finite Fibonacci words $f_n$, for natural numbers $n$, are the words in the letters $0$ and $1$ defined by $f_0 = 0$ and $f_{n+1} = \varphi(f_n)$, where $\varphi$ is the Fibonacci morphism, which replaces each letter $0$ by $01$ and each letter $1$ by $0$.
nodes.title: Finite Fibonacci words

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an infinite word over $\{0, 1\}$ and let $f_1, f_2, f_3, \ldots$ be finite words over $\{0, 1\}$ with $f_1 = 1$, $f_2 = 0$ and $f_{n+3} = f_{n+2} f_{n+1}$ for every natural number $n$, such that for every natural number $n$ the word $f_{n+2}$ consists of the first $|f_{n+2}|$ letters of $f$. nodes.title: The infinite Fibonacci word as $0$ followed by the finite Fibonacci words

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $t$ be finite words in the letters $0$ and $1$, and let $k$ be a natural number smaller than the length of $a$. Then the letter at position $k$ of the concatenation $a t$ equals the letter at position $k$ of $a$, counting positions from $0$.
nodes.title: Appending a word does not change earlier letters

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be the set of natural numbers obtained from $1$ by finitely many applications of the maps $x \mapsto 2x$ and $x \mapsto 4x - 1$. Let $S$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers whose set of values is $K$, and let $w$ be the binary sequence with $w(n) = 1$ if $S(n + 1)$ is odd and $w(n) = 0$ if $S(n + 1)$ is even. can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
